name: Mazdutide
lead: Mazdutide (also IBI362 and LY3305677) is a once-weekly injectable peptide that activates both the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor and the glucagon receptor. It was developed by Innovent Biologics together with Eli Lilly, and received marketing approval in China in June 2025.[1]

In a phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight, once-weekly mazdutide was reported to produce clinically relevant weight loss versus placebo.[2] Earlier trials and a meta-analysis reported weight loss in people with and without diabetes.[5][4] It is a prescription drug in China and investigational elsewhere; it appears in looksmaxxing discussions as a possible next-generation fat-loss peptide.

paras: Mazdutide has been studied for weight management in adults with overweight or obesity and for type 2 diabetes. A phase 3 trial randomised Chinese adults with a BMI of at least 28 (or overweight with other criteria) to mazdutide doses or placebo, and reported weight reduction with active treatment.[2] A phase 2 trial in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity ran 24 weeks of treatment up to 6 mg.[6]
In type 2 diabetes, a phase 2 trial evaluated mazdutide against placebo in adults managed with diet and exercise or stable metformin,[7] and a 2026 Nature report compared it with dulaglutide.[8]

A phase 1b trial reported up to 6.4% body weight loss over 12 weeks at doses up to 6 mg, and extended testing to 9 mg and 10 mg.[9] A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials has pooled mazdutide's effects on weight loss in diabetic and non-diabetic patients,[5] and network meta-analyses have placed it alongside other GLP-1 receptor agonists and polyagonists.[10] Most trial participants have been Chinese adults, so applicability to other populations has not been established in published trials.

Mazdutide combines GLP-1 receptor activation, which reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying, with glucagon receptor activation, which has been proposed to raise energy expenditure; it is described as an analogue of oxyntomodulin.[1][11][3]

Published trials describe gastrointestinal effects typical of the GLP-1 class.[2][9] Readers should consult the primary trial reports for event rates; long-term safety data beyond the phase 3 programme remain limited.
Mazdutide is approved only in China. Outside that market it is an investigational drug, and online discussions of it concern unapproved access. Specific sourcing is outside the scope of this wiki.

Registered trials are exploring mazdutide in conditions including fatty pancreas, polycystic ovary syndrome, gout with obesity, type 1 diabetes, coronary plaque, mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes, alcohol use disorder and cirrhosis-related portal hypertension.[12][13][14][15][16][17][18]

Human trials include a phase 3 trial in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight,[2] a phase 2 weight-loss trial,[6] a phase 1b multiple-ascending-dose trial,[9] a phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes,[7] and a comparison with dulaglutide.[8] A systematic review and meta-analysis pooled the weight-loss trials.[5]

card.summary: Weekly GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist approved in China for weight loss; strong trial data, but regional approval only.
card.note: Approved only in China; investigational elsewhere. Trials mostly in Chinese adults.

quick.overview:
Mazdutide is a once-weekly injection that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, developed by Innovent and Eli Lilly. It was approved for weight management in China in June 2025.

A phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight reported meaningful weight loss. Participants in most trials have been Chinese adults.
quick.mechanism: The GLP-1 component reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying; the glucagon component is proposed to increase energy expenditure.
quick.risks: Trials describe GI side effects typical of GLP-1 drugs. It is a prescription drug in China and investigational elsewhere, so use outside approved markets means unregulated supply.
